# dsbgv

> Computes all eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a real generalized symmetric-definite banded eigenproblem A_x = lambda_B_x.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dsbgv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dsbgv';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dsbgv(
    order,
    jobz, uplo,
    N, ka, kb,
    AB, LDAB,
    BB, LDBB,
    w, strideW,
    Z, LDZ,
    WORK
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ka` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super- (or sub-) diagonals of A<br>Requires `ka ≥ 0` |
| `kb` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super- (or sub-) diagonals of B<br>Rejects `kb < 0 \|\| kb > ka` |
| `AB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(ka + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · Band matrix A in band storage |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AB`<br>Column-major requires `LDAB ≥ ka + 1`<br>Row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `BB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(kb + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · Band matrix B in band storage |
| ↳ `LDBB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `BB`<br>Column-major requires `LDBB ≥ kb + 1`<br>Row-major requires `LDBB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | `w` stride length |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix for eigenvectors |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Z`<br>Rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldz < N)` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 3 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangles of A and B are stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangles of A and B are stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.
- `ka`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KA} \ge 0$.
- `kb`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix B if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KB} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric band matrix A, stored in the first ka+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(ka+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{ka}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{ka})$.

  On exit, the contents of `AB` are destroyed.
- `BB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric band matrix B, stored in the first kb+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of B is stored in the j-th column of the array `BB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `BB(kb+1+i-j,j) = B(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kb}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `BB(1+i-j,j) = B(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kb})$.

  On exit, the factor S from the split Cholesky factorization $B = S^T \, S$, as returned by DPBSTF.
- `w`: If `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, Z contains the matrix Z of eigenvectors, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. The eigenvectors are normalized so that $Z^T \, B \, Z = I$. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument is invalid (rejected when `kb < 0 \|\| kb > ka`)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `ka + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `kb + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < N )`)

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dsbgv.strided(
    jobz, uplo,
    N, ka, kb,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    BB, strideBB1, strideBB2, offsetBB,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ka` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super- (or sub-) diagonals of A<br>Requires `ka ≥ 0` |
| `kb` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super- (or sub-) diagonals of B<br>Rejects `kb < 0 \|\| kb > ka` |
| `AB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(ka + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · Band matrix A in band storage |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AB` |
| `BB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(kb + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · Band matrix B in band storage |
| ↳ `strideBB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `BB` |
| ↳ `strideBB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `BB` |
| ↳ `offsetBB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `BB` |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `w` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix for eigenvectors (N-by-N) |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Z` |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Z` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 3 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array (length >= 3\*N) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangles of A and B are stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangles of A and B are stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.
- `ka`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KA} \ge 0$.
- `kb`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix B if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KB} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric band matrix A, stored in the first ka+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(ka+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{ka}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{ka})$.

  On exit, the contents of `AB` are destroyed.
- `BB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric band matrix B, stored in the first kb+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of B is stored in the j-th column of the array `BB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `BB(kb+1+i-j,j) = B(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kb}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `BB(1+i-j,j) = B(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kb})$.

  On exit, the factor S from the split Cholesky factorization $B = S^T \, S$, as returned by DPBSTF.
- `w`: If `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, Z contains the matrix Z of eigenvectors, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. The eigenvectors are normalized so that $Z^T \, B \, Z = I$. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `kb < 0 \|\| kb > ka`)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, and i is: \<= N:  the algorithm failed to converge: i off-diagonal elements of an intermediate tridiagonal form did not converge to zero;
-   `> N`: if $\mathrm{INFO} = N + i$, for $1 \le i \le N$, then DPBSTF returned `INFO = i`: B is not positive definite. The factorization of B could not be completed and no eigenvalues or eigenvectors were computed.

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dsbgv()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DSBGV`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dsbgv.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dsbgv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dsbgv';

// 3x3 diagonal matrices (KA=KB=0), A = diag(5, 6, 7), B = diag(2, 3, 4):
const AB = new Float64Array( [ 5.0, 6.0, 7.0 ] );
const BB = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
const W = new Float64Array( 3 );
const Z = new Float64Array( 9 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 9 );

const info = dsbgv( 'column-major', 'compute-vectors', 'upper', 3, 0, 0, AB, 1, BB, 1, W, 1, Z, 3, WORK ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info );
console.log( 'Eigenvalues (W):', W );
console.log( 'Eigenvectors (Z):', Z );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSBGV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSBGV computes all the eigenvalues, and optionally, the eigenvectors of a real generalized symmetric-definite banded eigenproblem, of the form $A \, x=(\lambda ) \, B \, x$. Here A and B are assumed to be symmetric and banded, and B is also positive definite.

</section>
